analysis.title: Morning Briefing - Waller's forward guidance for December
key_insights: Fed voter Waller said a half-point rate increase may be needed in December if October core CPI comes in around 0.3% or higher. SG economics forecast core at 0.3% m/m against consensus of 0.2%.
Today's US CPI is the final CPI release before the December FOMC meeting, with one more PCE print to come. SG expects the market reaction to be larger than usual.
Brent fell below $90/b, down 23.5% from its October top, with its first daily close below the 200dma since 5 August. Lower oil is supporting European currencies, EUR rates and the INR and ZAR.
The S&P 500 erased its midterm election losses, led by tech (+2.7%). The US 10y yield fell 2.5bp to 4.858%, with support at 4.81% and resistance at 4.95%.

ECB chief economist Lane said it is prudent to hike in December as things stand, without relying on cheaper oil as a factor. He expects core and food inflation to quicken. SG notes the EUR 10y IRS ignored the hawkish comments.
BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli will not rule out voting for a rate rise in December but says she does not yet have enough information.

The PBoC raised the FX reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% a week ago. Chinese local banks are now raising USD deposit rates to above 4.0% on balances over $50k, about 120bp higher than a few months ago, while yuan deposit rates fell to about 0.95%. SG reads this as Beijing putting a floor under USD/CNY.

USD/INR fell below 94.00 for the first time since April, helped by lower oil and portfolio inflows (FPIs bought about INR80bn of FAR-eligible bonds and INR459.7bn of equities last week). The next leg lower depends on RBI tolerance for rupee strength given its large net short dollar position.
USD/ZAR is drifting toward its 200dma near 16.41 on lower oil, despite a weaker-than-expected ANC showing in municipal elections.
China's October trade surplus narrowed to $105.28bn, below forecast. Exports slowed to 35.2% y/y and imports rose to 41.6% y/y.
Norway October CPI rose to 3.6% y/y from 3.4%, while core slowed to 2.7% from 3.0%, the lowest since July.

macro_indicators.interpretation: SG forecasts a third straight 0.3% monthly gain, against consensus of 0.2%. Used cars rose 0.7% and apparel 0.3% last month, and relief in those categories could produce a softer print. A print at or above 0.3% is Waller's threshold for considering a 50bp hike in December.
Headline is expected at 0.3% m/m, with core as the focus for the December Fed decision.
Headline accelerated from 3.4% while core slowed from 3.0%, the lowest since July.
The surplus came in below forecast. Exports slowed to 35.2% y/y and imports rose to 41.6% y/y.
A four-year low, which weighs on AUD.
A six-year low, which weighs on AUD.

risk_factors: A core CPI print of 0.3% or higher could push the Fed toward a 50bp hike in December. Yields would rise, with the steepening selloff possibly concentrated in the long end.
Falling Brent is pulling back future inflation expectations, so the response of different parts of the curve to a firm print is uncertain.
The RBI's tolerance for further rupee appreciation limits USD/INR downside.
Weak Australian confidence and business surveys weigh on AUD.
charts_described: Chart of the day: US core CPI m/m from April to October 2026, with a 3-month average. The figure for the latest month is the SG forecast of 0.3%.
vol_and_positioning: The US midterm election losses in indices have been erased. The 14 October bid in bonds came with a Nasdaq drop of 1.9%, and SG expects the CPI reaction function to revert to normal.
geopolitical: Brent has fallen 23.5% from its October top and is below $90/b.
The PBoC raised the FX reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6%, and local banks are raising USD deposit rates to slow CNY appreciation.
The ANC underperformed expectations in South African municipal elections.

tension_points.theme: US core CPI and December Fed
tension_points.bull_case: A downside surprise to core CPI would give bulls fresh impetus to test the 100dma for US 10s at 4.81%, with bullish seasonal tailwinds possibly opening a move below 4.80%. Relief in used cars and apparel could produce a friendly print.
tension_points.bear_case: A core print of 0.3% or higher would put a 50bp December hike on the table per Waller, and yields should shift higher, possibly with a steepening selloff concentrated in the long end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print of 0.3% m/m or higher, which is Waller's threshold for contemplating a half-point hike in December.
